name: forge_backup
summary: Snapshot override/ (and the stock manifest) into a timestamped backup.
doc:
Snapshot override/ (and the stock manifest) into a timestamped backup.

Cheap and always safe. Taken automatically by forge_deploy, but run it by
hand before installing any third-party mod.

name: forge_build
summary: Report exactly what a deploy would write, with sizes and shas.
doc:
Report exactly what a deploy would write, with sizes and shas.

There is no packing step in KOTOR -- override/ takes loose files -- so
'build' here means: freeze and describe the change set. Always run
forge_verify after this and before deploying.

name: forge_deploy
summary: Copy everything in staging/ into the game's override/.
doc:
Copy everything in staging/ into the game's override/.

Two-phase: without confirm=True this only prints what it WOULD do.
Refuses while swkotor2.exe is running -- the engine reads override/ at
module load and a file swapped underneath it is a crash. Takes a backup
automatically before writing.

name: forge_revert
summary: Restore override/ from a backup. Blank `to` lists what is available.
doc:
Restore override/ from a backup. Blank `to` lists what is available.

This RESTORES THE WHOLE DIRECTORY: files added since the backup are
removed. Refuses while the game is running.

name: forge_scan
summary: What in override/ is NOT stock -- i.e. what mods are actually live.
doc: What in override/ is NOT stock -- i.e. what mods are actually live.

name: forge_selftest
summary: Prove PyKotor round-trips this install's formats byte-identically.
doc:
Prove PyKotor round-trips this install's formats byte-identically.

Reads a real resource of each type out of the game, writes it back to
bytes, and compares. A format that does NOT round-trip is a format this
server must not write -- the same proof gate er-forge uses before adding
param rows.

name: forge_snapshot
summary: Capture the CURRENT override/ as the stock baseline.
doc:
Capture the CURRENT override/ as the stock baseline.

Only ever run this on a clean, unmodded install -- everything present at
capture time becomes 'stock' forever, and forge_scan will stop reporting
it as a mod. Refuses to overwrite an existing manifest without confirm.

name: forge_status
summary: Where everything stands: install, override contents vs stock, staging,
doc:
Where everything stands: install, override contents vs stock, staging,
backups, and whether the game is running.

name: forge_verify
summary: Prove the staged files are well-formed BEFORE they reach the game.
doc:
Prove the staged files are well-formed BEFORE they reach the game.

Every staged file is re-parsed from disk with PyKotor according to its
extension. A file that cannot be re-read is a file that will crash the
engine, and this is the only cheap place to catch it.

expect_changed: comma-separated filenames you intend to change. Supplying
it turns the report into a PASS/FAIL verdict on the exact set.

name: forge_workspace
summary: Prepare (or reset) the working tree: workspace/, staging/, oracle/.
doc:
Prepare (or reset) the working tree: workspace/, staging/, oracle/.

staging/ is where edited files accumulate. Nothing in it touches the game
until forge_deploy(confirm=True). reset=True wipes staging -- use it to
abandon a half-finished change set.

name: mod_install
summary: Install a TSLPatcher mod headlessly via HoloPatcher.
doc:
Install a TSLPatcher mod headlessly via HoloPatcher.

Vortex flatly refuses this entire class of mod, and legacy TSLPatcher.exe
is a GUI-only Delphi binary -- HoloPatcher's `--install --console` is the
only scriptable path. Takes a backup first, always.

name: mod_validate
summary: Lint a TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher mod's changes.ini WITHOUT installing it.
doc:
Lint a TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher mod's changes.ini WITHOUT installing it.

Point this at a downloaded mod's folder (the one containing
`tslpatchdata`, or tslpatchdata itself). Tells you what the mod would do
to your 2DAs, dialog.tlk and GFFs before it does it -- which matters
because TSLPatcher mods edit shared tables in place and stack badly.

name: module_info
summary: List the game's modules, or the resources inside one.
doc:
List the game's modules, or the resources inside one.

Blank module = list all 246 module files with their area codes.

name: res_describe
sig: (resref: str, rtype: str, order: str = 'all') -> str
summary: Summarise one resource: where it resolves from, and its contents.
doc:
Summarise one resource: where it resolves from, and its contents.

Understands 2DA (shape + headers), TLK, GFF-family templates (fields),
ERF/RIM (contents), NCS (instruction count), TPC (dimensions).

name: res_find
sig: (query: str = '', restype_filter: str = '', location: str = 'all', limit: int = 60) -> str
summary: Find resources by ResRef substring.
doc:
Find resources by ResRef substring.

query:          substring, case-insensitive. Blank = sample everything.
restype_filter: comma-separated extensions, e.g. 'utc,uti' or '2da'.
location:       all | override | modules | chitin | texturepacks |
                music | sound | voice | lips

name: script_compile
sig: (source: str = '', source_file: str = '', out_name: str = '', confirm: bool = False) -> str
summary: Compile NSS source to NCS bytecode, in-process, and stage it.
doc:
Compile NSS source to NCS bytecode, in-process, and stage it.

Uses PyKotor's native compiler targeting K2. We deliberately never shell
out to nwnnsscomp: six mutually-incompatible builds of it exist and they
disagree on CLI syntax, which is why PyKotor identifies them by SHA-256.

Give either `source` (inline NSS) or `source_file` (a path). out_name is
the ResRef, e.g. 'k_my_script' -> staging/k_my_script.ncs.

name: script_decompile
summary: Disassemble a compiled NCS script from the game back to readable form.
doc: Disassemble a compiled NCS script from the game back to readable form.

name: stage_add
summary: Copy an arbitrary file into staging/ so it can be deployed to override/.
doc:
Copy an arbitrary file into staging/ so it can be deployed to override/.

For loose-file mods: textures (.tga/.tpc/.txi), models (.mdl/.mdx),
templates, anything override/ accepts.

name: stage_clear
summary: Empty staging/, abandoning the current change set.
doc: Empty staging/, abandoning the current change set.

name: tlk_find
sig: (text: str = '', strref: int = -1, limit: int = 25) -> str
summary: Search dialog.tlk. Give `text` to search, or `strref` for one entry.
doc: Search dialog.tlk. Give `text` to search, or `strref` for one entry.

name: toolchain
summary: What modding tools are installed, their versions, and what each is for.
doc: What modding tools are installed, their versions, and what each is for.

name: twoda_add_row
sig: (table: str, values: str, label: str = '', confirm: bool = False) -> str
summary: Append a row to a 2DA and stage it.
doc:
Append a row to a 2DA and stage it.

values: 'column=value,column=value,...' -- unlisted columns are blank.
Row-adding is the operation most likely to break a 2DA, so the table is
proved to round-trip byte-identically BEFORE any row is added; if it does
not, this refuses rather than risking the table.

name: twoda_edit
sig: (table: str, row: int, column: str, value: str, confirm: bool = False) -> str
summary: Change one cell in a 2DA and stage the result.
doc:
Change one cell in a 2DA and stage the result.

Reads the CURRENT effective table (override first, then chitin), edits it,
re-parses what it wrote, and drops it in staging/. The game is untouched
until forge_deploy. Without confirm=True it reports the before/after only.

name: twoda_query
sig: (table: str, columns: str = '', where: str = '', limit: int = 30) -> str
summary: Read rows from a 2DA.
doc:
Read rows from a 2DA.

table:   e.g. 'appearance', 'baseitems', 'feat', 'spells', 'itempropdef'
columns: comma-separated column names. Blank = first 6 columns.
where:   'column=substring' filter, case-insensitive. Blank = from the top.
